title: Bon anniversaire, ma chérie!  (Happy Birthday, Darling!)

segments.t: Today is Camille's twenty-third birthday. As she rides the metro and arrives at the ASK office, her family calls to wish her a happy birthday, receptionist Sofia prepares for her own small role opposite JoeyStarr, and Mathias hands Camille an envelope without realizing what day it is. Listen to the scene in French first; don't worry about catching every word.
J'essaierai de descendre un week-end bientôt.
J'ai une scène avec JoeyStarr, je dois vraiment me concentrer.
Merci, Mamie. C'est vraiment une belle attention.
Je te rappelle, Mamie, d'accord? Gros bisous!
Le rapport du ministère sur le financement du cinéma. Pour Andréa.
Let's go back through it step by step. On the morning metro, Camille's phone rings with a birthday call from her mother.
'Hello? Thank you, Mum.' This special greeting used only when answering the telephone.
'Stop it! I have work here.' Her mother wants her to come home and work at her hair salon instead of staying at her father's agency in Paris.
J'essaierai de descendre un week-end bientôt.
'I'll try to come down for a weekend soon.' The simple future of 'to try', followed by the action word 'to go down' — how French speakers talk about travelling south from Paris to the provinces.
'Mum, that's enough!' As Camille walks into ASK and greets a handsome colleague, her mother teases her over the line.
'Hi, Camille.' At the reception desk, Sofia is getting ready to head out to the country film shoot.
J'ai une scène avec JoeyStarr, je dois vraiment me concentrer.
'I have a scene with JoeyStarr, I really have to focus.' Sofia has landed a two-line part as a servant in the eighteenth-century film.
'Do you want an autograph?' Sofia tries to sound casual as she heads out.
'Yours?' The possessive pronoun meaning 'yours', masculine singular to match 'autograph'.
'No, JoeyStarr's.' Literally 'the one of JoeyStarr' — French uses this demonstrative pronoun instead of adding an apostrophe-s.
'Yes, of course. See you later!' The short casual farewell at the end means 'until more'.
Merci, Mamie. C'est vraiment une belle attention.
'Thank you, Gran. That's really a lovely thought.' Upstairs at her desk, Camille takes a second birthday call from her grandmother, who has sent her a cheque in the post.
'Camille, do you have a moment?' Mathias steps out of his office holding a large envelope.
Je te rappelle, Mamie, d'accord? Gros bisous!
'I'll call you back, Gran, okay? Big kisses!' French uses the present tense 'I call you back' for an immediate promise.
'What is this?' As Mathias hands her the envelope, Camille hopes for a second that her father remembered her birthday.
Le rapport du ministère sur le financement du cinéma. Pour Andréa.
'The ministry report on cinema funding. For Andréa.' Mathias has completely forgotten what day it is.
'What is the matter?' Literally 'what is it that there is?'. Mathias notices the disappointment on her face.
'No, nothing. It's for Andréa.' Camille hides her hurt as Colette, watching from down the corridor, notices the strange tension between them.
J'essaierai de descendre un week-end bientôt.
J'ai une scène avec JoeyStarr, je dois vraiment me concentrer.
Merci, Mamie. C'est vraiment une belle attention.
Je te rappelle, Mamie, d'accord? Gros bisous!
Le rapport du ministère sur le financement du cinéma. Pour Andréa.

Mathias has completely forgotten Camille's twenty-third birthday, and Colette — watching from down the corridor — notices the strange tension between them as she investigates his file. See you next time!
